🥬 When to plant amaranth (efo tete) in Nigeria

Also called Ẹ̀fọ́ tẹ̀tẹ̀ (Yoruba) and Alayyahu (Hausa).

Quick answer: Plant amaranth (efo tete) in Nigeria from March to October and harvest from April to November. Sown all through the rains (year-round with watering). Ready in 3–5 weeks.

PlantMarch to October
HarvestApril to November
Grows inAll regions
TypeLeafy vegetables
Local namesẸ̀fọ́ tẹ̀tẹ̀ · Alayyahu

About amaranth (efo tete)

Amaranth is one of the fastest cash crops for small gardens and is used for efo riro.

How to plant amaranth (efo tete) well

Sow in batches every 2–3 weeks for a steady supply.

Sown all through the rains (year-round with watering). Ready in 3–5 weeks.

Diseases and pests of amaranth (efo tete)

  • Damping-off & wet rotDon't overwater seedlings and give good drainage.
  • Leaf caterpillarsHand-pick or use recommended controls.

Best states for amaranth (efo tete)

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant amaranth (efo tete) in Nigeria?

Plant amaranth (efo tete) in Nigeria from March to October and harvest from April to November. Sown all through the rains (year-round with watering). Ready in 3–5 weeks.

What is amaranth (efo tete) called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Amaranth (Efo tete) is called Ẹ̀fọ́ tẹ̀tẹ̀ (Yoruba) and Alayyahu (Hausa).

When is amaranth (efo tete) harvested in Nigeria?

Amaranth (Efo tete) is usually harvested from April to November.

Which Nigerian states grow the most amaranth (efo tete)?

Oyo, Lagos, Ogun, Kano, Kaduna, Enugu and Plateau are among the best-known amaranth (efo tete) states.

Can I grow amaranth (efo tete) in my part of Nigeria?

Yes. Amaranth (Efo tete) grows in every region of Nigeria: North and South.

What diseases attack amaranth (efo tete) and how do I prevent them?

Damping-off & wet rot: Don't overwater seedlings and give good drainage. Leaf caterpillars: Hand-pick or use recommended controls.
